title: Minor Sentences 簡略句／零碎句
titleZh: Minor Sentences 簡略句／零碎句

source.file: Sentence Structure 231 - Minor Sentences 簡略句／零碎句.pdf
omissions: Every numbered Important Rule and Benefit is retained as a separate Chinese-primary card. Where the PDF has no complete English counterpart, the English explanation is a faithful editorial translation.
The source filename is numbered 231; it is assigned system ID ss232 because the source set contains two distinct PDFs labelled 201.

formula: Context + concise expression without a full subject-verb structure

meaning.zh: 簡略句雖然沒有一般完整句子的主語和動詞結構，但在清楚語境中仍可傳達完整意思。

rules.zh: 簡略句省略的內容必須能夠從語境中清楚推斷。 A: Where is the receipt? B: No idea. （甲：收據在哪裏？） （乙：不知道。） The listener understands that No idea means: I have no idea where the receipt is.
rules.en: A minor sentence must be understandable from the context. For example, “No idea” can mean “I have no idea where the receipt is” when the question supplies that context.

rules.zh: 甲：我們可以在五分鐘內完成嗎？） （乙：沒可能。）
rules.en: A minor sentence can be a complete reply, such as “No chance” in answer to an unrealistic suggestion.
A minor sentence can appear before an explanation: “No problem. I can help you.”

rules.zh: 我傳送了錯誤的附件。是我的錯。）
rules.en: A minor sentence can appear after a complete sentence: “I sent the wrong attachment. My mistake.”

rules.zh: 告示寫得很清楚：禁止進入。）
rules.en: A minor sentence can appear after a colon: “The notice was clear: No entry.”
A minor sentence can appear inside direct speech: “No comment,” the director replied.

rules.zh: 在對話、標誌、筆記或有意營造語氣的文章中，簡略句可以是正確而自然的表達。 但是，在正式作文中，如果學生無意中遺漏必要的主語或動詞，便可能形成錯誤的殘缺句。 Intentional and clear: Too late. The train has already left. （太遲了。火車已經開走。） Accidental and unclear: Because the train had already left. 這一句只有原因，沒有完整主句，因此在一般正式寫作中是不完整的。
rules.en: Intentional minor sentences differ from accidental fragments. They are clear in dialogue, signs, notes or deliberate stylistic writing; an unintentionally incomplete subordinate clause is still an error in formal writing.

benefits.zh: 讓日常對話更自然 英語母語使用者在語境清楚時，通常不會重複所有已知資料。 A: Do you know where Leo went? B: I have no idea where Leo went. 這個回答符合文法，但有不必要的重複。 更自然的回答是： A: Do you know where Leo went? B: No idea.
benefits.en: It makes everyday conversation more natural by avoiding repetition of information already supplied by the context.

benefits.zh: 幫助你更快作出回應 簡略句可以讓你不用臨時組織一個長而完整的句子，也能迅速表達態度、反應或答案。 例如： Good idea. （好主意。） Not yet. （還未。） Maybe later. （也許遲些吧。）
benefits.en: It helps you respond quickly without constructing a long full sentence.

benefits.zh: 避免重複語境中已經清楚的內容 當對方已經說明人物、事件或問題時，你可以只保留真正重要的新資訊。 A: Have the results been announced? B: Not yet. 你不需要重複： The results have not been announced yet.
benefits.en: It avoids repeating content that the other speaker or the surrounding text has already made clear.

benefits.zh: 加強語氣和節奏 把簡略句放在完整句子之前或之後，可以令重點更加突出。 Too late. The doors have already closed. （太遲了。大門已經關上。） The doors have already closed. Too late. （大門已經關上。太遲了。） 兩個版本的基本意思相同，但重點和節奏略有不同。
benefits.en: It strengthens emphasis and rhythm when placed before or after a complete sentence.

benefits.zh: 適合多種真實情境 簡略句常見於： ● 日常對話； ● 電影及故事對白； ● 即時訊息； ● 標誌及告示； ● 標題； ● 筆記； ● 廣告； ● 簡短指示。 學會這些形式，有助你理解真實英語，而不只是課本中的完整句子。
benefits.en: It is useful in real contexts such as conversation, dialogue, messaging, signs, notices, headlines, notes, advertisements and short instructions.

benefits.zh: 增加句式變化 你不需要把所有句子都寫成相同的主語加動詞結構。 The plan failed. It was a real shame. 也可以寫成： The plan failed. A real shame. 第二個版本更簡潔，亦帶有較明顯的個人反應。
benefits.en: It increases sentence variety and can express a concise personal reaction more directly.

en: Rewrite each situation with the appropriate minor sentence shown by the context and first-word hint.
Keep the intended meaning concise and natural.

保留原意，並使答案簡潔自然。

questions.prompt: A: Can we complete this five-hour task in ten minutes? B: There is no possibility of that.

questions.promptZh: 甲：我們仍然可以進入戲院嗎？）（乙：不可以，因為大門已經關上。
